campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council agenda for October 6, 2026 lists items related to transitioning legal services as the city attorney position changes, along with decisions on pay and working conditions for several groups of non-union city employees. The agenda also includes a proposed market-based salary adjustment for the city manager.
keyTopics: Temporary legal services arrangements during the city attorney transition
Compensation and working conditions for unrepresented confidential, classified management, and unclassified management employees
Market adjustment to the city manager's salary

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's October 7, 2026 agenda covers routine items like meeting minutes, check registers, and a treasurer's report, alongside several larger decisions. These include a $2,500,000 budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation project, a new no-parking zone on Chester Avenue, a decision on the city's long-term law enforcement provider, a review of animal care service options, and a public hearing on annual updates to the City Code.
keyTopics: Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project budget amendment for $2,500,000
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for Chester Avenue near Arcadia Palms Drive
Discussion and determination of long-term law enforcement provider, including a possible agreement with Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
Comparison of regional animal care providers, including whether to continue with San Jose Animal Care and Services
Public hearing on annual City Code updates covering appeals scheduling and City Commissioner qualifications

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council agenda for September 22, 2026 included routine items like approving prior meeting minutes and a wastewater treatment plant agreement, along with a Councilmember's reappointment to the VTA Board. Notably, the agenda also listed an interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities, several city commission appointments, and an amendment to the city's legal services contract.
keyTopics: Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities and custodial-processing facilities
Commission appointments for the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Councilmember Jonathan Weinberg's authorized two-year reappointment to the VTA Board
Amendment No. 1 to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, setting a $21,500 monthly retainer

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's October 6, 2026 agenda covers routine business, including approving prior meeting minutes, financial reports, and payroll. It also includes a bid issue with a tree services contractor, a purchasing policy update, and the Finance Commission's revised annual work plan.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First Amendment to an existing agreement (Town Manager authorization)
Updated Finance Commission 2026 Work Plan
Resolution amending the Town's Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 7, 2026
san-jose.summary: This is a planning and administrative meeting of San José's Rules and Open Government Committee. The agenda listed review of a draft October 20, 2026 agenda, a public records summary, a city auditor activity report, and a few specific items including a Taiwan Retrocession Day proclamation and a proposal on self-checkout safety standards at grocery and drug stores. The regular October 13 City Council meeting was canceled; a separate joint special meeting with the Santa Clara Valley Water District Board remains scheduled that day.
keyTopics: Review and adjustment of the draft October 20, 2026 City Council agenda
Joint City of San José and Santa Clara Valley Water District special meeting item
City Auditor's monthly report of activities for September 2026
Proclamation and special event approval for Taiwan Retrocession Day (sponsored by Council District 5)
Proposal on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores (Candelas and Cohen)

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: This Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee agenda covers the city's draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan and the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory. The agenda also includes a general opportunity for public comment and a standing section for committee and staff updates.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council's October 6, 2026 agenda includes several recognitions, routine approvals, and two notable public hearings: one on new rules restricting potable water use for nonfunctional turf irrigation, and another considering a Service Worker Retention Ordinance. The agenda also lists a public art proposal for the Lakewood Park renovation and various informational reports on completed council projects.
keyTopics: Public hearing on an ordinance to prohibit potable water irrigation of nonfunctional turf, implementing state law AB 1572
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation
Amending a purchase agreement with WSP USA Inc. for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill
Recognitions for the 2026 Sunnyvale Little League Junior Division All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 6, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council's agenda for this meeting includes a closed session on anticipated litigation and on real estate negotiations with the Cupertino Union School District over the Finch Avenue property, followed by a public meeting with routine items and two items related to The Rise development. Consent calendar items cover meeting minutes, treasurer's reports, retiree health insurance contributions, and a grant application, alongside a property exchange agreement for the Finch site.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with the Cupertino Union School District
Approval of an exchange agreement for the Finch property at a negotiated purchase price of $11.8 million
Resolution increasing employer contributions for retiree medical and hospitalization insurance under PEMHCA for pre-August 2004 hires
Resolution authorizing an $80,000 grant application for the Rubberized Pavement Grant Program
Public information session on the approved soil contamination remediation plan at The Rise, plus a TEFRA public hearing on conduit financing for the project

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent — October 6, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This combined Santa Clara City Council and Stadium Authority Board agenda includes a joint dinner meeting with the Parks and Recreation Commission, several proclamations, routine consent items, and a public hearing on pedestrian access restrictions near Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways. The agenda also lists a staff presentation on data center development policy and several council member requests related to data centers, parking, and towing issues from stadium events.
keyTopics: Report and potential Council action on pedestrian access restrictions on portions of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways
Staff presentation on updating city policies for new data center development, including water usage and grid support participation
Council requests on data center regulation, including a potential moratorium on standalone data centers and a ban on non-disclosure agreements with data center developers
Council requests on resident parking near apartment complexes and possible compensation for vehicles ticketed or towed during stadium events
Proclamations for Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and United Against Hate Week

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council agenda for September 15, 2026 covers a mix of financial and community items, including a federal housing grant plan, a review of the city's red light camera program, and a look at the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The agenda also includes bond-related actions tied to the former Redevelopment Agency's Successor Agency.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency board
Resolution authorizing sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — October 2, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee's agenda for this meeting includes staff and committee member comments, plus an update on electric system long duration resiliency. The agenda notes this item is classified as 'Not a Project' under CEQA, meaning it falls outside that environmental review process.
keyTopics: Update on Electric System Long Duration Resiliency
CEQA determination for the resiliency item: Not a Project
Staff presentation on the resiliency update
